content.title: About
content.content: Ice Cream Sundae (NFS 457) is a classic dessert consisting of a vanilla ice‑cream scoop topped with chocolate sauce, chopped nuts, a cherry, and whipped cream. Served in a tall glass, it creates a layered visual effect.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first sundae appeared in the United States in the 1930s and quickly became a fast‑food staple.
The name “sundae” derives from the day of the week—Sunday—when restaurants offered a special treat.
The original recipe used only chocolate sauce and a cherry; nuts were added later for crunch.
In different countries a sundae may include caramel, caramelized banana, or sea salt.
In 2020 NFS released a limited “Sundae 457” edition featuring sea salt and caramel crumbles.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: The dairy base provides calcium essential for bone health.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: Sugar and fat deliver quick energy when consumed in moderation.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Dairy contains vitamin B12, important for the nervous system.

items.title: Antioxidants in chocolate sauce
items.content: Dark chocolate is rich in flavonoids that may support cardiovascular health.

items.title: Fiber from nuts
items.content: Nuts add a small amount of dietary fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Large portions can raise blood glucose levels.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: The ice cream contains lactose, which may cause discomfort for intolerant individuals.

items.title: Nut allergy
items.content: Added nuts can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The combination of ice cream, sauce, and cream makes the dessert calorie‑rich; moderation is key.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the sundae immediately after assembly so the sauce stays fluid. You can add fresh berries, sprinkle cinnamon, or drizzle caramel to taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the frozen product at –18 °C or lower. Once thawed, consume within 2‑3 hours, otherwise the texture may change.
